messages:
lucy_support: quick heads up — EU customer (org: eu-acme) hit 403s on embeddings/search after we rotated their org API key a few hours ago. generation endpoints (v2/generate) are returning 200 with the new key, embeddings return 403 with "invalid_scope" in the body. they say some worker jobs still use the old key.
eline_sre: thx. do we have their request headers / example curl? need Authorization header and any X-Region or X-Edge headers.
lucy_support: pasted from customer (redacted):
```
curl -i https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \\ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED_KEY>" \\ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\ 
  -d '{"model":"embed-small","input":"hi"}'
```
response: 403 {"error":"invalid_scope","detail":"embedding.create not allowed for key"}
eline_sre: interesting — that error is from authz check (scope mismatch) not a raw 401. Two hypotheses: 1) their old key was revoked but some components cached a key->scope map and are still consulting an old mapping (rare), or 2) they actually have two different key objects in Vault/KV (one mounted into CI as env, one in Vault path) and some jobs are using the rotated-but-still-active key with reduced scopes.
matt_oncall: i dug into logs for eu-acme: we see interleaved requests from two key fingerprints. One fingerprint shows up as newly provisioned with full scopes, the other as a rotated key with embed scope removed (looks like a scoped rotate we suggested). Timestamp ordering shows batch workers making requests from containers started before rotation.
support_l2: repro steps i used locally:
1) create a scoped key via console (embed disabled)
2) call generate -> 403? no, generate used a different key and works
3) call embedding -> 403 with same error.
So behaviour matches. Root cause for customer: some runners still have the old env image pointing to the rotated key object (same label but different secret payload).
sre-bot: incident created: INC-2026-0885 assigned to @eline_sre, severity: sev3, customer impact: partial (embeddings/search).
eline_sre: mitigation notes — quick checklist we gave customer: 1) verify which key the process is sending (log Authorization header fingerprint or short-kid). 2) restart any long-lived processes or cronworkers so they pick up new env secret. kubectl example: `kubectl rollout restart deploy -l app=eu-acme-worker -n eu-acme`. 3) if they mount secrets via Vault agent sidecar, ensure agent refreshed token: `kubectl exec -c vault-agent $POD -- vault agent -config=/etc/vault/agent.hcl` OR restart sidecar pod. 4) revoke the old key in console only after all consumers have restarted.
support_l2: also added this edge purge step because customer uses private edge cache: POST to https://edge.redwood.ai/internal/purge with JSON `{"scope_fingerprint":"<fp>"}` — that clears any cached authz mapping for ~30s.
lucy_support: customer tried restart of web pods but missed the batch job fleet (k8s job set). they restarted those and embeddings started returning 200. customer confirmed in logs they see new kid fingerprint `kid:eu-9a3f` after restart.
eline_sre: root cause summary for ticket: rotation created new key object with different scope set; some consumers were still running with containers/processes that referenced the rotated key secret path (or older image with baked env var). those processes continued to call embedding endpoints which require explicit embed scope and therefore failed. action items: - docs update: note rotation must be accompanied by worker restarts if secrets are injected at process startup. - add automated check to console to warn when rotating keys with scope changes (detect running pods referencing secret path).
matt_oncall: leaving a note — for future: we can add a health-check endpoint that fails on auth mismatch so fleet managers can autorestart before keys are revoked. filing follow-up RFC.
support_l2: customer satisfied, will keep ticket open until 24h of stable metrics. closing steps saved to INC-2026-0885. :white_check_mark:
